Staff recommends that the City Council:

Receive and file emergency procurement report on emergency procurement with Los Angeles County Sanitation Districts – Puente Hills Material Recycling Facility for emergency landfill disposal services for the Public Works Department. B. Approve Acceptance of Environmental Protection Agency Grant and Purchase of Street Sweepers for the Resource Recovery and Recycling Division
R ecommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Adopt a finding of Categorical Exemption pursuant to Section 15302 (Replacement or Reconstruction) of the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) guidelines;
2. Authorize the City Manager to accept a grant awarded in the amount of
$945,000 from the United States Environmental Protection Agency for the Clean Heavy-Duty Vehicles Grant Program for the City of Santa Monica Street Sweeper Replacement Project in the Public Works Department, and to accept all grant renewals;
3. Authorize the City Manager to execute all necessary documents to accept the grant, all grant renewals, and modifications;
4. Authorize the Procurement Manager to issue a purchase order with Municipal Maintenance Equipment (“MME”), a California-based company, for the purchase of three Ravo Electric R5-eSeries sweepers for the Public Works Department, Resource Recovery and Recycling Division. This recommended award is made as an exception to the competitive bidding process pursuant to Section 2.24.250 (c) and is for a total amount not to exceed $2,428,833 including a 10% contingency;
5. Authorize the Procurement Manager to issue a purchase order with Mar-co Equipment Company for the purchase of one Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Tymco Model 600 sweeper for the Public Works Department, Resource Recovery and Recycling Division. This recommended award is made as an exception to the competitive bidding process pursuant to Section 2.24.250 (c) and is for a total amount not to exceed $185,987 including a 10% contingency with future year funding contingent on Council budget approval; and
6. Authorize budget amendment as outlined in the Financial Impacts & Budget Actions section of this report (requires 5 votes).
If the grant is not received, pending the outcome of the Presidential Executive Order:
7. Authorize the Procurement Manager to issue a purchase order with Mar-co Equipment Company for the purchase of two Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Tymco Model 600 sweepers for the Public Works Department, Resource Recovery and Recycling Division. This recommended award is made as an exception to the competitive bidding process pursuant to Section 2.24.250 (c) and is for a total amount not to exceed $996,976 including a 10% contingency with future year funding contingent on Council budget approval.

R ecommended Action
Staff recommends that the City Council:
1. Declare City-owned properties located at Bergamot Station Arts Center located at 2500 Olympic (APNs 4268-013-919 and 4268-014-900) as “surplus land” within the meaning of the Surplus Land Act (Government Code sections 54220 et. seq.) (“SLA”) , adopt a resolution declaring the Bergamot Station Arts Center as surplus land , authorize the City Manager or his or her designee to advance the Notice/Request for Proposal (RFP) by June 30, 2025 and take implementing actions nece ssary to comply with the SLA and the City’s Housing Element .
2. Declare two City-owned properties located at 1333 4 th Street (APNs 4291-011- 909 and 4291-011-910) and 1324 5 th Street (APNs 4291-011-900, 4291-011-901, 4291-011-902, 4291-011-903, 4291-011-904, 4291-011-905 and 4291-011- 908) as “surplus land” within the meaning of the SLA , adopt a resolution declaring the 4 th /5 th and Arizona as surplus land , authorize the City Manager or his or her designee to advance the Notice/Request for Proposal (RFP) by June 30, 2027 and take implementing actions necessary to comply with the S LA and the City’s Housing Element .
3. Declare City-owned property at 1234 4 th Street (currently operated as a public parking structure , Parking Structure 1 , (PS1) as “exempt surplus land” within the meaning of the SLA; a uthorize staff to begin the process of obtaining necessary permits, including a Coastal Development Permit, for demolition of PS1 if demolition is approved by the California Coastal Commission, authorize staff to proceed with develop ing bidding documents for the demolition to prepare the site for a future 100% affordable housing development.

  CITY OF SANTA MONICA

  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES

  FEBRUARY 25, 2025

  A regular meeting of the Santa Monica City Council was called to order by Mayor Negrete at 5:31 p.m., on
  Tuesday, February 25, 2025, at City Council Chambers, 1685 Main Street, Santa Monica, CA.

  members present except Mayor Pro Tem Torosis. Councilmember Hall led

  STATEMENT OF  The City of Santa Monica is located on the land of Tovangaar. With
  ACCOUNTABILITY  great respect, the City acknowledges the Gabrieleño/Tongva as the First
  (LAND  People of this ancestral and unceded territory of Kuruvungna, a village
  ACKNOWLEDGEMENT)  that we know as Santa Monica. We honor their elders, past and present,
  and the Gabrieleño descendants who are part of the Gabrieleño /Tongva
  tribes.

  We recognize that these peoples are still here, and as settlers and kuyam
  (guests), we recognize our responsibility and obligation to care for their
  land in partnership with them. The City of Santa Monica commits to
  work in partnership with the Gabrieleño/Tongva people to uplift their
  voices and visibility on their ancestral land.

  The City of Santa Monica Statement of Accountability (Land
  Acknowledgement) was read into the record by Councilmember
  Zernitskaya.

  STAFF  11.A. Adoption of Resolution No. 11646 (CCS) and Approval of
  ADMINISTRATIVE  Release of Request for Proposals for City-Owned Sites Designated for
  ITEMS:  Affordable Housing Development in the City's 6th Cycle Housing
  AFFORDABLE HOUSING  Element and Declaration of Sites as "Exempt Surplus Land" in
  DEVELOPMENT  Accordance with the Surplus Land Act, was presented and adopted.

  Recommended Action
  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Declare City-owned properties located at Bergamot Station Arts
  Center located at 2500 Olympic (APNs 4268-013-919 and 4268-014-
  900) as “surplus land” within the meaning of the Surplus Land Act
  (Government Code sections 54220 et. seq.)(“SLA”), adopt a
  resolution declaring the Bergamot Station Arts Center as surplus
  land, authorize the City Manager or his or her designee to advance
  the Notice/Request for Proposal (RFP) by June 30, 2025 and take
  implementing actions necessary to comply with the SLA and the
  City’s Housing Element.
  2. Declare two City-owned properties located at 1333 4th Street (APNs
  4291-011- 909 and 4291-011-910) and 1324 5th Street (APNs 4291-
  011-900, 4291-011-901, 4291-011-902, 4291-011-903, 4291-011-
  904, 4291-011-905 and 4291-011-908) as “surplus land” within the
  meaning of the SLA, adopt a resolution declaring the 4th/5th and
  Arizona as surplus land, authorize the City Manager or his or her
  designee to advance the Notice/Request for Proposal (RFP) by June
  30, 2027 and take implementing actions necessary to comply with the
  SLA and the City’s Housing Element.
  3. Declare City-owned property at 1234 4th Street (currently operated
  as a public parking structure, Parking Structure 1,(PS1) as “exempt
  surplus land” within the meaning of the SLA; authorize staff to begin

  the process of obtaining necessary permits, including a Coastal

  by the California Coastal Commission, authorize staff to proceed
  with developing bidding documents for the demolition to prepare the
  site for a future 100% affordable housing development.
  4. Adopt the findings stated in the Environmental Review section of this
  staff report, including, without limitation, a finding of categorical
  exemption pursuant to Section 15312 of the California
  Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Guidelines, a finding of no
  possibility of significant effect on the environment pursuant to
  Section 15061(b)(3) (Common Sense Exemption), and a finding that
  the development of affordable housing on City-owned property was
  previously analyzed in the 6th Cycle Housing Element
  Environmental Impact Report.

  Questions asked and answered of staff included is there any reason why both
  loans can’t expire in 2028; would the City retain ownership of the land; why
  is it not an option to sell PS1 at any use; would it be wise to list PS1 as
  surplus instead of exempt surplus; is there an option to deviate from the
  previous Council’s decision in regard to 4th/5th and Arizona and Bergamot
  Station; is the City obliged to transfer units to other sites if they can't build
  an exact number of units; why is the staff recommendation to look at
  Bergamot Station before the 4th/5th and Arizona site; what are the limitations
  on what can be included in the RFP as preferences at Bergamot; could the
  City make preferences for a project that would allow existing gallery and
  other arts and cultural use tenants to return when it's redeveloped; could it be
  included in the RFP to permit flexibility to include market rate units to help
  subsidize some of the other things that we would want in that type of project;
  is Bergamot fully leased and what are the current revenues from the site; if
  the recommended process and timing is approved to issue the initial RFP for
  Bergamot by June 2026, what would happen then; how long would the RFP
  be open and when would anything happen on the site; under the RFP process,
  would the city retain ownership of the land, or would that be transferred to
  whoever would develop it; if both tenants at 4th/5th and Arizona were to
  extend their leases through 2030, how could that affect our commitment to
  meeting RHNA goals and staying compliant with our housing element; if we
  allowed the tenants to extend their leases through 2030, would we possibly
  have a shovel ready project or something by the time the leases end; what is
  the City’s history with permitting parking by parishioners of St. Augustine
  by the Sea and what is the City’s obligation; how would city staff be able to
  allocate additional resources to handle both RFPs for Bergamot and 4th/5th
  and Arizona at the same time; what are the tradeoffs that would have to be
  made if we wanted to advance both of these RFPs and on a similar time
  frame; what potential risks would the city face if it waited until 2027 to
  release the 4th/5th and Arizona RFP, especially considering market
  conditions and funding uncertainties; given our need for revenue, could

  4th/5th and Arizona be structured as mixed-use development to allow for
  revenue generating uses at that site; have we measured the staffing needs and
  the need to delay 4th/5th for two years with the need for future downtown
  economic development and activation of our downtown area; what impact
  would a delayed RFP have on future activation of our downtown area; can a
  phased approach be used with these two RFPs to ensure that both projects
  move forward simultaneously, but on somewhat of a staggered timeline, so
  that we're not competing for the same tax credits; instead of selling PS1,
  could we put PS1 out to an RFP, as is, without investing any additional
  money; could we put out PS1 to RFP, see what comes back and maintain
  ownership of the land, but give site control, or some sort of long term ground
  lease to a third party who would either maintain and generate some revenue,
  redevelop, or tear down the site, so the city would not have to pay to
  seismically retrofit or demolish the site; does staff think that a creative
  developer would come forward with a revenue generating option for the site
  that would absolve the city of any financial obligation on this site; in order
  to dispose of PS1 would we have to list it as surplus first;; what is the current
  height limit on 4th/5th and Arizona; and is PS1 only seismically safe until
  2027.

  Considerable discussion ensued on topics including, but not limited
  viewing any of the current uses as surplus; the prioritization of projects;
  engagement with the stakeholders in downtown Santa Monica; the need to
  be cognizant of tradeoffs between immediate financial return from these
  lease holds and the bang for the buck we get from revitalizing downtown;
  merit in moving forward with the 4th/5th and Arizona site first; trying to use
  a staggered approach; having more revenue from the sites while we find a
  good potential project in light of the city's current budgetary issues; desires
  for items to be included in the RFP for Bergamot, such as, a preference for
  right of return, or at least right of first refusal for current tenants, looking at
  how we could potentially temporarily relocate current tenants so we don't
  lose those arts and cultural resources within the city, allowing for some
  flexibility so that we could have some market rate units to help subsidize
  some of the things that we would like to see, allowing for creative uses that
  make it a really great community gathering spot; combining PS1 and the
  4th/5th and Arizona project as surplus land and putting it out for RFP
  together to allow some flexibility, but to give preference to the Bergamot
  Station RFP; the importance of being realistic with these very important
  complex projects; the lack of availability for state grants or local sources of
  funding to assist with completing these projects; needing to have to involve
  interesting commercial revenue generating uses on the sites; listing all of
  these projects as surplus and putting them out as soon as possible this year,
  as opposed to waiting; and getting revenue for the next three years by
  extending both bank leases through 2028.
